text:
Alex: Heads-up — repro of OOMs on long streaming jobs when using AWQ + fp8 + large batch spikes. Seen on staging with gptx-7B-awq.
Maria: repro steps?
Alex: run the >16k token stream test with concurrent 8x small requests (1-4 tokens). Memory climbs then OOMs around kv-cache flush boundaries.
Jamal: I ran profiler. Main offenders: transient workspace allocations from mixed kernel selection + KV cache dtype copies. When kernel chooser switches to fp8-fused attention for some layers we allocate temp fp32 buffers for matmuls, then cast -> fragmentation.
Sophie: so the allocator fragmentation + temporary upcasts are the issue, not raw KV size?
Alex: yes. KV raw is large but stable. The spikes are ephemeral: per-request workspace peaks that the slab allocator can't pack due to fragmentation. Also our KV materializer was eager-upcasting AWQ-backed KV to fp32 on write.
Ryan: any numbers from the trace?
Jamal: captured a 90s run. Peak alloc 42GB -> OOM. After changes (soft-reserve + lazy-upcast) peak was 34.2GB. ~18% peak reduction. p50 latency +0.9ms, p95 +6ms on worst case, but throughput steady.
Maria: explain soft-reserve?
Alex: small change to allocator: keep a configurable soft-reserve region per-device that prevents immediate full consumption by transient allocations; it triggers kernel-switch or request backpressure before hard OOM. It also cooperates with the workspace pool.
Sophie: workspace pool details?
Alex: introduced a global transient buffer pool for the runtime thread that reuses same-sized buffers across requests and kernels. Pool slices are 64KB-aligned; we reuse instead of free/alloc for short-lived buffers. This dramatically reduces fragmentation.
InfraBot: deploy /staging apply: allocator.soft_reserve=0.08
Ryan: how did we handle AWQ KV dtype?
Jamal: changed materialization to lazy-upcast-on-read: keep KV stored in AWQ's compact format in device memory; only upcast to fp32 on attention compute if kernel requires fp32. If fp8 kernel available we feed directly. This cut redundant copies.
Maria: are there perf regressions due to extra branching and on-the-fly upcast?
Jamal: microbenchmarks: upcast-on-read adds ~0.5ms per attention when upcast occurs, but most model configs had fp8-capable kernels so path avoided. Overall win because we removed a global copy on every request.
Alex: we also added a dynamic kernel selector extension: it predicts memory headroom for next N tokens and prefers memory-frugal kernel variants when headroom low. It's a soft policy — it only switches if predicted extra latency < threshold.
Sophie: how's prediction done?
Alex: sliding-window of recent allocation deltas + simple moving average of per-token mem delta, multiplied by expected seq length. Cheap and effective.
Ryan: any config snippet we should use for testing?
Alex: here's what I used in staging:

```
allocator:
  type: soft_slab
  soft_reserve: 0.08        # fraction of device mem to keep as headroom
  pool:
    enabled: true
    slice_size: 65536
kernel_router:
  mem_aware_threshold_ms: 5
  mem_aware_window_tokens: 16
kv:
  materialize_strategy: lazy_upcast_on_read
  store_dtype: awq_compact
```

Maria: nice. Did you add metrics/traces to track these decisions?
Jamal: yes — new traces: alloc.fragmentation_pct, kernel.switch_count, kv.upcast_count, pool.reuse_ratio. I pushed a Grafana dash for the staging cluster.
InfraBot: grafana link: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/runtime-awq-allocator
Sophie: any edge cases? long-running streams with incremental context growth?
Alex: we saw a case where repeated partial-rollbacks + canary kernel-switch churned pool buffers and caused temporary regression. Fix is to debounce kernel-switches per request and favor pool reuse for same-request kernels.
Ryan: what's next for prod rollout?
Maria: plan: 1) 48h soak on staging with mixed AWQ/FP8 models 2) enable on canary subset of customers (5%) with verbose tracing 3) watch alloc fragmentation and kv.upcast_count 4) full rollout if stable.
Jamal: adding an escape hatch flag to forcibly prefer fp8-kernel-only routing for low-memory machines.
Sophie: update the docs? PMs need a note about potential tiny p95 hit.
Alex: will write short doc and add to runbook. Also adding a small selftest in infra that runs the 16k streaming scenario nightly.
Ryan: thanks team — big win if we can avoid OOMs without heavy quant changes.
Maria: agreed. :tada:
Alex: tl;dr: soft-reserve allocator + transient pool + lazy kv upcast + mem-aware kernel routing = ~18% peak mem reduction, small latency tradeoff in worst cases.
Jamal: I'll keep trimming extra copies and look at more aggressive pool compaction next.
Sophie: great work.
InfraBot: rollout job queued for canary cluster.
Alex: merging PRs now: #4213 #4218. anyone object?
Maria: LGTM.
Ryan: LGTM.
Sophie: ok from me.
Alex: thanks — closing thread.
